mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 QoQ decline does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals robust economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO YoY increase does not correlate with subsequent economic expansion.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and CPI (CPIAUCSL) YoY is below 2%, the real interest rate is high, signaling a restrictive monetary policy that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of high FEDFUNDS and low CPIAUCSL YoY does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% YoY signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST YoY decline does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of instances with PAYEMS increase > 200,000, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by less than 1% QoQ and housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 5% YoY, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of low GDPC1 growth and HOUST decline does not correlate with subsequent negative returns.
